clue.text: Small motor hired out to cardinal

parts.note: a motor is a car
to let property is to hire it out

explanation.surface: A small car has been rented to a senior Roman Catholic churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' looks like the churchman of the surface, but here it is the bright red colour named after his robes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal red is a vivid crimson shade, the hue of a cardinal's vestments.

clue.text: Son and parent take one's breath away

parts.note: a mother is a parent

explanation.surface: A boy and his mum leave someone breathless.
explanation.definitionFit: To suffocate someone is literally to stop their breathing.

clue.text: George, Otto, Paul, Tim involved with CIA

indicators.note: involved suggests the names are tangled up together and rearranged

explanation.surface: Four men named George, Otto, Paul and Tim get mixed up with American intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George' looks like a fifth name in the list, but it is RAF slang for the device that flies an aircraft on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen nicknamed an aircraft's autopilot George.

clue.text: Abandoned port

definitions.meaning: deserted, gone away from
the ...-hand side of a ship facing forward

explanation.surface: A harbour that has been deserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserted is a past participle sense; port is the nautical term for the side opposite starboard.

clue.text: Couple use a stopwatch to deceive

parts.note: a couple is two
to time something is to measure its duration with a watch

explanation.surface: A pair measures a race in order to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: To two-time is to be unfaithful to a partner, deceiving them.

clue.text: Fellow-doctor needs tidy hair

parts.note: co- means fellow or joint, as in co-worker
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A colleague in medicine needs to neaten their hairdo.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a toothed implement through hair is to neaten it.

clue.text: Happen to get detached

definitions.meaning: to take place, as a planned event does
to fall away, as a button might

explanation.surface: Something occurs so that a part becomes loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A planned event takes place; a loose part falls away: both are the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Mould in the grape juice

definitions.meaning: mustiness or mould
unfermented juice pressed from grapes for winemaking

explanation.surface: Fungus growing in the freshly pressed wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Winemakers name unfermented pressed juice so; mustiness is the dank smell of mould.

clue.text: Drive around Islington to get a TV screen

indicators.note: around has the drive's word enclose the postcode letters

parts.note: to motor is to drive
Islington, in north London, has the postcode N1, read as NI

explanation.surface: A trip round an inner London district to buy a television.
explanation.walkthrough: Islington's London postcode is N1, taken here as the letters N and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A display unit for a computer or television is called this.

clue.text: Record border before one country exhibits ethnic prejudice

indicators.note: before puts the border ahead of the remaining pieces

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
a rim is an edge or border
I is the Roman numeral for one
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: Documented frontier policies of a country show racial bias.
explanation.definitionFit: Unjust treatment of people on grounds of race or ethnicity is this kind of bias.

clue.text: Not in service. Cashiered?

definitions.meaning: unavailable for use, like a broken machine
an officer cashiered is dismissed, so stripped of the rank granted by their warrant

explanation.surface: A dismissed officer is no longer serving.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: unusable, or an officer who has lost his commission, the document conferring rank.

clue.text: Male representative needs fibre

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
an MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

explanation.surface: A male politician needs more roughage in his diet.
explanation.definitionFit: This plant yields a coarse fibre used for rope and sacking.

clue.text: Suddenly discover that a pop song is playing

definitions.meaning: to come upon an idea by chance
a hit is a successful song, and on means being played

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles on a chart-topper on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means stumble upon; split, it says a chart success is being broadcast.

clue.text: Tax firm in small street

indicators.note: in places the firm's letters inside the abbreviated street

parts.note: St is the short form of Street
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A tax levied on a firm based in a little street.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOT is an old word for a tax, surviving in the phrase 'scot-free'.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a scot was a levy or municipal payment, hence escaping one was going scot-free.

clue.text: A nicotine addict would die without it!

definitions.text: A nicotine addict would die without it!

parts.words: A nicotine addict would die without it!
parts.note: tobacco users take powdered tobacco through the nose; and the slang verb for dying adds the pronoun 'it'

explanation.surface: Someone hooked on tobacco cannot live without their fix.
explanation.walkthrough: Powdered tobacco is sniffed; and 'snuff it' is slang for die, so 'die without it' is the phrase minus 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Powdered tobacco inhaled through the nose, and the verb in the slang phrase for dying.

clue.text: Reserved for skating

definitions.meaning: kept in waiting, postponed for later
on a frozen surface, where skaters go

explanation.surface: A rink has been booked for skaters.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans kept in abeyance are put in cold storage; skating takes place on a frozen surface.

clue.text: Train about to return military group to the East

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: return says the military group's word is read backwards

parts.note: a unit is a military formation
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A soldiers' detachment is sent back eastward on the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns UNIT into TINU. 'Train' looks like the railway, but it is the entourage following a dignitary.
explanation.definitionFit: A train is the body of attendants following an important person, an entourage.

clue.text: Not as plain to a pigeon enthusiast, maybe

definitions.meaning: more ornate, the comparative of fancy
someone who breeds or keeps birds or animals as a hobby, pigeons being one example

explanation.surface: Someone tells a pigeon breeder that the birds are less ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is more elaborate; the other is a hobbyist who breeds animals, as in pigeon-fancying.

clue.text: To get a match is the very devil

definitions.meaning: an old type of friction match
Satan, the fallen angel

explanation.surface: Finding something to strike a light is maddeningly hard.
explanation.definitionFit: An early friction match bore the same name as the fallen angel Satan.

clue.text: Will beneficiary give note to ambassador?

parts.note: a legate is an envoy or ambassador, especially of the Pope
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the envoy will hand over a message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' reads as the future auxiliary, but it is a testament: the definition is someone who inherits.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who receives a bequest under a testament is the heir to that legacy.

clue.text: Correct uniform for sappers

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps whose soldiers are called sappers
dress is a uniform, as in full dress

explanation.surface: The right uniform for military engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To put right a wrong is to remedy it, the verb sense.

clue.text: Such a sale is fashionable indeed

annotationWithheld.why: Such a sale is fashionable indeed (7): the parse is U (fashionable) in ACTION (deed), with 'indeed' doing two jobs, both the insertion indicator 'in' and the fodder 'deed'
annotationWithheld.clue: Such a sale is fashionable indeed

clue.text: Disconcerted a wicked woman within

indicators.note: within places the woman inside the word for wicked

parts.note: bad means wicked
she is the female pronoun, a woman

explanation.surface: Someone is embarrassed by a wicked woman inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling embarrassed or put out is a synonym for the definition.

clue.text: Something one should smell in merry mood

definitions.text: Something one should smell in merry mood

parts.words: Something one should smell in merry mood
parts.note: a small bunch of flowers meant to be sniffed; split, the item is the organ of smell plus a word for cheerful

explanation.surface: Sniffing something while in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue hints at the organ you smell with followed by an old word for merry.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fragrant bunch of flowers, a posy, is held up to sniff.

clue.text: One is carried in a gun carriage

indicators.note: is carried in places the letter for one inside the gun

parts.note: gat is slang for a gun
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single item is transported in a gun carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gun carriage' reads as one military object, but 'gun' gives GAT and 'carriage' is the definition, meaning how someone walks.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage is the way a person holds and moves their body, their bearing when walking.

clue.text: I pine for Platonic perfection

parts.note: deal is softwood timber such as pine

explanation.surface: A philosopher longs for the perfect forms of Plato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like the verb 'long', but it is the wood: DEAL is pine or fir timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato's theory of forms holds that perfect archetypes exist beyond the physical world.

clue.text: Lots of trousers

definitions.meaning: ... of something means plenty of it
Oxford ... are wide-legged trousers

explanation.surface: Plenty of pairs of trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the word means plenty; it also names loose-fitting slacks, as in Oxford bags.

clue.text: Some of the Arab leaders are talented

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of the Arab rulers are gifted.
explanation.definitionFit: Being skilled or competent is a synonym for being talented.

clue.text: Necklace with a Catholic dedication

parts.note: to is the word used in a dedication, as in 'to my wife'
RC is the abbreviation for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: A pendant chain inscribed to a Roman Catholic.
explanation.walkthrough: A torc is a rigid twisted metal neck ring worn by ancient Celts.
explanation.definitionFit: A torc is a Celtic neck ornament, a rigid metal collar.

clue.text: Fault-finding when there are problems using a horn

parts.note: troubles are problems
hooting is sounding a car horn

explanation.surface: Diagnosing a car fault when the horn keeps sounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracing and fixing faults in a system is what this diagnostic activity means.

clue.text: A county where people retire

definitions.meaning: The short form of Bedfordshire, an English county north of London
to retire is to go to bed for the night

explanation.surface: A shire where folk go to spend their old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retire' suggests leaving work, but it means going to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedfordshire is abbreviated thus, and sleeping furniture is where you go when retiring at night.

clue.text: After last month encyclopaedia displays propriety

indicators.note: After places the encyclopaedia's abbreviation following the month

parts.note: Dec is December, the year's final month
ency is a recognised abbreviation for encyclopaedia

explanation.surface: Following December, a reference work shows good manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean conformity with accepted standards of good behaviour.
